title: Measuring the Marginal Value of Sandboxed Emulation for Validator‑Checked LLM‑Generated NetOps Artifacts
abstract: We preregistered and executed a paired confirmatory study (study_id f2c3d8b1-7a6e-4a9a-b2c3-5f8e1d2b6c7e) that measured the marginal detection benefit of adding sandboxed emulation to a deterministic validator for LLM-generated intent→configuration artifacts. Using shared_initial_candidate semantics with the declared model "gpt-5-mini" (provider: openai_responses), we evaluated 720 paired tasks drawn from three topology templates and three abstract vendor‑CLI families. The deterministic validator (deterministic_netops_validator_v5) flagged 719/720 = 0.9986111111; the guarded pipeline (validator + sandboxed emulation, plus an allowed repair stage) flagged 720/720 = 1.0. The paired difference (guarded − baseline) = 0.0013888889; exact McNemar two‑sided p = 1.0; 95% bootstrap percentile CI (10000 resamples, seed = 1729) = [0.0, 0.0041666667]. Provider-call accounting: model_calls_used = 721 (720 shared initial + 1 repair-stage call). These results lie far below our preregistered minimum effect-of-interest (0.20). We report the preregistered design, artifact-grounded counts and inferential outputs, an explicit clarification of provider-call audit fields, and an evidence‑based interpretation that the negligible guarded benefit in this regime stems from a validator ceiling effect, curated parser-validated inputs, and shared_initial_candidate semantics. We identify operational boundary conditions where guarded stages are likely to add value and point readers to the archived execution manifest for full machine-verifiable artifacts.

sections.introduction: Generative large language models (LLMs) are increasingly proposed to translate operator intent into device configuration and NetOps workflows. Operational adoption hinges on reliable detection of syntactic, ordering, and higher‑order safety/policy violations in generated artifacts. A common mitigation architecture is generate→validate→(repair)→execute, and many system reports recommend layering sandboxed emulation after static validation to reveal runtime-only faults. Prior surveys and tool reports document this practice but provide limited large-scale, preregistered paired measures of the marginal value added by sandboxed emulation when a strong static validator is already present. Motivated by that gap, we preregistered and executed a controlled paired experiment to answer this research question: under shared_initial_candidate semantics, what is the paired detection-rate difference (guarded − baseline) between (A) a deterministic validator alone and (B) the same validator followed by automated sandboxed emulation (plus the permissive, preregistered repair allowance)? Our contributions are (1) a machine-readable preregistration and faithful autonomous execution; (2) an artifact-grounded paired analysis on Npairs = 720 with complete accounting; (3) a concise method-level clarification of provider-call auditing that resolves apparent accounting asymmetries; and (4) an evidence-based interpretation identifying boundary conditions in which guarded stages are—and are not—operationally helpful.
sections.related_work: Work on LLMs for NetOps emphasizes that correctness is multidimensional and that generation must be paired with verification and, in some systems, emulation or execution harnesses [1]. Tool-focused analyses (e.g., the evolution of Batfish-like static verifiers) show steady expansion of rule-sets and topology-aware checks but identify remaining gaps for runtime-dependent behaviors; this motivates layering emulation after static validation in practice [2]. Prototype systems that combine generation with validation and sandboxed execution report heterogeneous gains: emulation catches runtime semantics in some regimes but often provides marginal benefit where validators already cover task patterns [3]. Our paired, shared_initial_candidate design isolates only downstream guarded-stage signals (emulation or repair) and thus complements prior literature by providing an artifact-grounded estimate of guarded-stage marginal contribution under conservative generation semantics.
sections.methodology:
Preregistration and primary estimand. We preregistered a paired-binary confirmatory design (study_id f2c3d8b1-7a6e-4a9a-b2c3-5f8e1d2b6c7e). The primary estimand is the paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline aggregated across confirmatory samples. The preregistered plan targeted Npairs = 720 (planned episodes = 1440) with a minimum effect-of-interest = 0.20 for power planning. Inclusion/exclusion, missingness handling (deterministic reseed up to two times for parser failures), and multiplicity handling for exploratory analyses were fixed before execution.

Task bank, topology templates, and shared_initial_candidate semantics. Confirmatory items were deterministically generated from a structured task family that embeds initial_state, expected_final_state, an explicit intent, required_command_sequence, allowed_touched_fields, and workflow policies (e.g., make-before-break). The bank covers three abstract vendor‑CLI families and three topology templates (leaf–spine, 3-node service chain, triangle). For each pair the pipeline performed exactly one shared initial model call (one sampled candidate) that was used unchanged by both downstream conditions. This shared_initial_candidate enforcement removes generation variability as a cause of between-condition discordance and isolates only downstream guarded-stage effects (emulation observations or repair-stage activity).

Validator, guarded pipeline, and repair policy. The baseline validator (deterministic_netops_validator_v5) applies deterministic vendor-CLI parsing, per-command canonicalization, sequence-order checks against the required_command_sequence, atomicity/workflow constraints, group-level invariants, and final-state conformance tests. The guarded pipeline runs the validator and then executes the candidate in a sandboxed emulation harness that instantiates the declared topology and executes normalized CLI commands against vendor‑abstracted virtual devices; the harness reports runtime observations that are mapped to guarded detections when they reveal policy or safety violations not encoded as validator rules. The preregistered repair policy allowed at most one repair-stage model invocation per task (repair calls are permitted only after the shared initial generation and after validator/emulation observations are available for the guarded condition). All repair calls and transcripts were archived.

Provider-call auditing and reconciliation (clarification). Some readers may find the execution audit summary superficially asymmetric (e.g., condition_counts showing different numeric values). To avoid confusion we explicitly clarify the audited fields and show how they reconcile with pair accounting: (1) model_calls_used is the total hosted-model call count recorded for the run (artifact-grounded value: 721). (2) stage_counts partitions model calls by the logical pipeline stage: shared_initial_generation = 720 (one initial generation per pair) and repair = 1 (the single repair-stage call invoked in the guarded condition across all pairs). (3) condition_counts in the audit refer to provider-call events attributable to labeled stages (the audit labels shown in the manifest include a key named "shared" that corresponds to the shared_initial_generation stage and a key labeled "guarded" that in this run corresponds to repair-stage calls executed only for the guarded condition). Because shared_initial_generation produced 720 provider calls and the guarded repair stage produced 1 provider call, the audit shows counts {shared:720, guarded:1} even though complete_pair_count = 720. In short: the provider-call audit asymmetry reflects stage-level provider calls (720 initial shared calls + 1 repair call = model_calls_used 721) while pair accounting (complete_pair_count = 720) remains correct and paired. The archived deterministic reconciliation and provider-call audit artifacts record these values and were the authoritative input to analysis.

Analysis procedures. The preregistered primary analysis used a paired-binary executor aligned with McNemar inference and produced an exact McNemar two‑sided p-value plus a 95% paired-bootstrap percentile CI (10000 resamples, bootstrap_seed = 1729). The primary analysis used complete-pair handling per preregistration; no irrecoverable technical pairs occurred in the confirmatory run.
sections.results:
Artifact-grounded confirmatory counts and inferential outputs. Complete_pair_count = 720. Contingency counts: n11 = 719 (detected by both), n10 = 1 (guarded-only), n01 = 0 (baseline-only), n00 = 0 (neither). Marginal detection rates: baseline = 719/720 = 0.9986111111111111; guarded = 720/720 = 1.0. Paired difference (guarded − baseline) = 0.001388888888888884. Exact McNemar two‑sided test p = 1.0. 95% bootstrap percentile CI (10000 resamples, seed = 1729) = [0.0, 0.004166666666666667]. These numeric values are verbatim from the archived analysis artifacts and analysis/results.json.

Provider-call and repair accounting (artifact-grounded). The run used model_calls_used = 721 (720 shared initial + 1 repair-stage call) as recorded in the execution manifest. Because shared_initial_candidate semantics were enforced, the single n10 discordant pair must be attributable to either (i) a guarded-emulation runtime observation not codified as a validator rule or (ii) the single recorded repair-stage invocation. The archived reconciliation links that unique discordant pair to the single repair-stage call; auditors can confirm this mapping in the canonical execution manifest and raw results archive. No irrecoverable parser or emulation failures occurred (failed_episode_count = 0), so the confirmatory analysis rests on a complete paired sample.

Representative episode diagnostics. Representative per-episode validator_trace artifacts show parsed_command_count, required_command_count, and violation_count fields; for the majority of episodes violation_count = 0 and validation_before/after states confirm final-state conformance. Those representative artifacts illustrate that most shared_initial candidates satisfied the validator’s rule set and that sandboxed emulation corroborated validator findings in this curated task bank.
sections.discussion:
Artifact-grounded interpretation. The negligible guarded-stage aggregate benefit in this run is explained most parsimoniously by three artifact-evidenced factors: (1) validator ceiling effect: the deterministic validator explicitly encoded the workflow patterns exercised by the curated tasks, producing a baseline success rate of 719/720 (0.9986) and leaving essentially no headroom for emulation to add detections; (2) curated parser-validated inputs: inclusion required vendor-parser acceptance and deterministic task generation produced inputs aligned with validator-covered patterns, reducing the prevalence of runtime-only faults; (3) shared_initial_candidate semantics and low repair activity: reusing the identical sampled candidate for both conditions isolates downstream signals and, in our run, only a single repair-stage call occurred (repair = 1), accounting for the unique discordant episode.

Operational implications. For pipelines that enforce strong parser-level prevalidation and maintain a high-coverage deterministic validator tuned to expected intent families, automated sandboxed emulation may yield negligible incremental detection benefit relative to its cost. Conversely, in operational regimes characterized by noisy natural-language intents, adversarial or fuzzed inputs, larger vendor diversity, or longer-lived stateful procedures, guarded emulation is more likely to reveal violations that static rules miss. We therefore recommend a risk‑tiered deployment: invest in validator coverage for routine, low-risk changes; selectively apply guarded emulation for high‑impact changes or for validation of out-of-distribution intents; and seed validator expansion with adversarial task banks to find systematic gaps.

Limitations tied to the archived evidence. The finding is narrowly scoped: it applies to the deterministic task bank used, the single validator implementation, the declared/requested model, the enforced shared_initial_candidate semantics, and the emulation fidelity exercised. The study was powered to detect a 0.20 absolute paired difference; the observed effect (~0.0014) lies far below that sensitivity and should be interpreted as a constrained near-zero result for the selected regime, not a general negative claim about guarded pipelines across all NetOps settings.
sections.conclusion: We preregistered and executed an artifact‑grounded paired confirmatory study comparing a strong deterministic validator with the same validator augmented by sandboxed emulation on a curated synthetic intent→configuration bank. Over 720 paired tasks the guarded pipeline produced a vanishing aggregate detection gain (0.0013888889) with exact McNemar p = 1.0 and 95% bootstrap CI [0.0, 0.0041666667]. Provider-call accounting shows model_calls_used = 721 and a single repair-stage invocation corresponding to the single guarded-only detection; archived reconciliation links that discordant pair to the repair call. We interpret the negligible marginal benefit as arising from a validator ceiling effect and curated parser-validated inputs under shared_initial_candidate semantics. Follow-up work should target adversarial and production-like task banks, expanded vendor diversity, multi-validator ensembles, and higher-fidelity emulation to identify regimes where guarded stages provide substantive operational value.

limitations: Synthetic task bank and deterministic task generator produce limited ecological diversity and can induce a validator-ceiling effect; results may not generalize to noisier, adversarial, or production distributions.
Single declared/requested model family (gpt-5-mini) and single validator implementation (deterministic_netops_validator_v5) limit generalizability across models and validator families.

Preregistered shared_initial_candidate semantics (one initial generation reused across paired conditions) isolate guarded-stage contribution but remove between-condition generation variability; this design constrains discordance sources to downstream guarded-stage observations or repair calls.

Sandboxed-emulation fidelity relative to vendor/OS production behaviors and long-lived control-plane subtleties is limited by the emulation harness used; higher-fidelity emulators could change outcomes in other regimes.

Study power planning targeted a minimum detectable paired difference of 0.20; the observed aggregate effect (~0.0014) lies far below that design sensitivity and should be interpreted as a narrowly scoped near-zero finding for this experimental regime.
